How the pieces fit together. Read this before adding a feature.

- [1. Repo layout](#1-repo-layout)
- [2. Package topology](#2-package-topology)
- [3. Manifest + entry points](#3-manifest--entry-points)
- [4. Build pipeline](#4-build-pipeline)
- [5. Storage layers](#5-storage-layers)
- [6. State stores](#6-state-stores)
- [7. File ingest flows](#7-file-ingest-flows)
- [8. `file://` interception flow](#8-file-interception-flow)
- [9. FSA (File System Access) lifecycle](#9-fsa-file-system-access-lifecycle)
- [10. Tabs + URL sync + hash nav](#10-tabs--url-sync--hash-nav)
- [11. Rendering pipelines](#11-rendering-pipelines)

- [19. Known constraints](#19-known-constraints)
- [20. Adding a new feature — checklist](#20-adding-a-new-feature--checklist)

---

## 1. Repo layout

```
file-viewer/
├── apps/
│   └── chrome-ext/                          MV3 extension — the host
│       ├── public/
│       │   ├── manifest.json                MV3 manifest
│       │   └── icons/
│       ├── src/
│       │   ├── app/                         Main viewer tab (?file=…, ?intercept=…)
│       │   │   ├── index.html               entry: app
│       │   │   ├── main.tsx
│       │   │   ├── App.tsx                  root + hydrate orchestration
│       │   │   ├── shell/                   TopBar, Sidebar, TabStrip, Viewer, …
│       │   │   ├── adapters/                Chrome-specific StorageAdapter + AssetResolver
│       │   │   ├── store.ts                 zustand library store (files/folders/tabs/ui)
│       │   │   ├── settings.ts              zustand settings store (formats/json/shortcuts)
│       │   │   ├── urlSync.ts               ?file=<id> two-way URL sync
│       │   │   ├── registry.ts              ext → Renderer component mapping
│       │   │   ├── fs.ts                    FSA helpers (pickFolder, walkDirectory, …)
│       │   │   ├── sessionHandles.ts        in-memory FSA handle registry (per tab)
│       │   │   ├── intercept.ts              picks up the content-script payload
│       │   │   └── welcomeDoc.ts             first-run markdown content
│       │   ├── options/                      chrome_options_ui page
│       │   │   ├── index.html                entry: options
│       │   │   ├── main.tsx
│       │   │   └── OptionsApp.tsx
│       │   ├── content/
│       │   │   └── handler.ts                content script (file:// URL interception)
│       │   ├── background/
│       │   │   └── service-worker.ts         dev WS reload + action.onClicked
│       │   ├── components/ui/                shadcn / basecn primitives
│       │   ├── lib/utils.ts                  cn() helper
│       │   └── styles/index.css              design tokens + mdx body typography
│       ├── vite.config.ts
│       └── package.json
├── packages/
│   ├── viewer-core/                          @file-viewer/core — shared types + ThemeProvider
│   ├── mdx-viewer/                           @file-viewer/mdx — Markdown / MDX renderer
│   └── json-viewer/                          @file-viewer/json — JSON / JSONC renderer
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── CLAUDE.md                                 session rules (extends global rules)
├── TASKS.md                                  living task list
└── ARCHITECTURE.md                           this doc
```

## 2. Package topology

Three publishable viewer packages + a host. The host depends on all three;
the viewers depend only on `@file-viewer/core`.

```
              @file-viewer/core
              ▲               ▲
              │               │
              │               │
   @file-viewer/mdx      @file-viewer/json
              ▲               ▲
              │               │
              └──────┬────────┘
                     │
                apps/chrome-ext
```

Each viewer package obeys the **portability contract** (see
[CLAUDE.md](./CLAUDE.md) for enforcement): no `chrome.*`, no `vscode.*`,
no Node built-ins. Host-specific concerns arrive through
`ViewerProps`.

```ts
// packages/viewer-core/src/types.ts
export interface ViewerProps {
  content: string;           // file contents as text
  file: FileRef;             // id, name, ext, path, sourceUrl?
  storage?: StorageAdapter;  // host storage (IDB in chrome-ext)
  assets?: AssetResolver;    // resolves relative image paths
  onNavigate?: (href: string) => void;
  trust?: "full" | "safe";   // MDX JSX evaluation posture (v0.2+)
}
```

## 3. Manifest + entry points

`apps/chrome-ext/public/manifest.json` exposes:

| Key | Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `manifest_version` | 3 | MV3 is mandatory for new Web Store submissions |
| `action` | `{ default_title }` | Toolbar icon → service worker opens the viewer tab |
| `background.service_worker` | `service-worker.js` (module) | Dev WS reload + icon click |
| `content_scripts` | `content.js` on `file:///*` | `file://` URL interception |
| `options_ui` | `src/options/index.html`, `open_in_tab: true` | Settings page |
| `permissions` | `["storage"]` | chrome.storage.sync + session |
| `web_accessible_resources` | `src/app/index.html`, `assets/*` matched on `file:///*` + `<all_urls>` | Lets the content script redirect `file://` → extension tab |

Four bundle entries go through Vite (`vite.config.ts`):

| Entry | Output | Consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | `src/app/index.html` + hashed assets | viewer tab |
| `options` | `src/options/index.html` + hashed assets | options page |
| `service-worker` | `service-worker.js` (fixed name) | background worker |
| `content` | `content.js` (fixed name, IIFE) | content script |

The fixed filenames for `service-worker.js` and `content.js` are pinned in
`vite.config.ts:entryFileNames` because `manifest.json` references them
by name. **If you rename one you must rename the other.**

## 4. Build pipeline

Three stages, each filtered via pnpm workspaces:

```
pnpm --filter @file-viewer/core  build   # tsup → dist/{index.js,.d.ts}
pnpm --filter @file-viewer/mdx   build   # tsup → dist/{index.js,.d.ts}
pnpm --filter @file-viewer/json  build   # tsup → dist/{index.js,.d.ts}
pnpm --filter chrome-ext         build   # tsc --noEmit && vite build
```

`pnpm build` at root runs all of them in order via `pnpm -r`.

`pnpm dev` watches the chrome-ext bundle; a tiny Vite plugin
(`extensionReload` in `vite.config.ts`) starts a WebSocket on
`ws://localhost:8791`, pings "reload" after each rebuild, and both the
service worker + the main page listen and call `chrome.runtime.reload()`
/ `location.reload()` respectively.

## 5. Storage layers

| Layer | Lives | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chrome.storage.sync` | Chrome cloud, ~100 KB cap, cross-profile | User settings (`useSettings`) — via `settings.ts` helper with IDB fallback |
| `chrome.storage.session` | Per-browser-session, in-memory | `file://` interception payload ferry (content script → viewer tab) |
| IndexedDB (`file-viewer` db, `kv` store) | Per-origin, large | Library state: files, folders, tabs, theme, UI prefs, settings mirror, task-list state, FSA handles |
| `sessionStorage` | Per-tab | Content-script re-entry guard (`fv-handled`) |
| In-memory (`sessionHandles`) | Per tab | Live FSA handles (not serializable) |

### IDB keys

```
lib:files       Record<id, LibraryFile>     all known files (incl. folder children + drop files + intercepts)
lib:folders     Record<id, LibraryFolder>   without handle / fileHandles (session-only)
lib:recent      string[]                    Recent list, stable order
lib:tabs        string[]                    Open tabs, stable order
lib:active      string | null               active tab
lib:theme       ThemeSettings
lib:ui          { sidebarOpen, tocOpen, fullscreen, autoRefresh, autoRefreshMs }
fsa:handle:<id> FileSystemDirectoryHandle   FSA handle per folder (idb-keyval serializes it)
fv:task:<id>    Record<number, boolean>     task-list checkbox state per file
fv:settings     Settings                    mirror of chrome.storage.sync (fallback only)
```

### settings.ts precedence

`chrome.storage.sync` first; on write, both stores are updated; on read,
sync wins and IDB is only used when sync is unavailable.

## 6. State stores

Two zustand stores, each with `hydrate()` called once in `App.tsx`:

### `useLibrary` (`apps/chrome-ext/src/app/store.ts`)

```ts
{
  files, folders,                 // IDB-persisted
  openTabs[], activeFileId,       // IDB-persisted
  recentIds[],                    // IDB-persisted
  theme,                          // IDB-persisted
  sidebarOpen, tocOpen,
  fullscreen,
  autoRefresh, autoRefreshMs,     // UI prefs bucket in IDB
  viewMode: "rendered" | "raw",   // session-only
  sessionRev: number,             // bump to force re-check of sessionHandles
  hydrated: boolean,
}
```

### `useSettings` (`apps/chrome-ext/src/app/settings.ts`)

```ts
{
  settings: {
    formats:            { md, mdx, json, jsonc },     // per-format enable
    json:               { theme, collapsedDepth, … }, // react-json-view opts
    shortcuts:          Partial<Record<ShortcutId, boolean>>,
    allShortcutsDisabled: boolean,
  },
  hydrated: boolean,
}
```

`useSettings.hydrate()` also registers a `chrome.storage.onChanged`
listener for live cross-tab updates: change a setting on the options
page and the viewer tab reacts without a reload.

## 7. File ingest flows

Three entry points, converging on the same `useLibrary` store shape:

```
┌──────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐
│ drag / drop  │  │ Open Folder btn │  │ file:// URL navigation │
│  (DropZone)  │  │  (TopBar)       │  │ (content script)       │
└──────┬───────┘  └────────┬────────┘  └───────────┬────────────┘
       │                   │                       │
       ▼                   ▼                       ▼
  readDroppedFile     pickFolder             chrome.storage.session
  + text/uri-list     + FSA handle +         + redirect to
  match               walkDirectory          ?intercept=<key>
       │                   │                       │
       └───────────────────┴───────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                  useLibrary.addFiles()
                  useLibrary.addFolder()
                           │
                           ▼
                      setActive(id)
                           │
                           ▼
            openTabs updated, URL synced,
            Viewer re-renders with new file
```

### Drop files

`DropZone.onDrop`:

1. Reads `dataTransfer.items[].webkitGetAsEntry()` to detect directories
   (files show up via `dataTransfer.files`).
2. For loose files: matches each to an entry in
   `dataTransfer.getData("text/uri-list")` (Finder / Explorer populate
   this with `file://` URLs). If matched → `sourceUrl` auto-set.
3. For dirs: recursive `walkDirEntry()` reads every supported file into
   memory; `rootPath` auto-set from text/uri-list. Registers as
   `LibraryFolder.kind = "drop"` (no FSA handle, no reconnect dance).
4. Each file's `ext` is run through `isFormatEnabled(settings, ext)`;
   disabled formats are skipped.

### Open Folder

`fs.ts:pickFolder()`:

1. `window.showDirectoryPicker({mode: "read"})` → directory handle.
2. Persist handle to IDB under `fsa:handle:<id>`.
3. `walkDirectory(handle)` → list of supported file entries.
4. Register session handles via `sessionHandles.register(…)`.
5. `useLibrary.addFolder(folder, files)` with `kind: "fsa"`.

## 8. `file://` interception flow

The golden path for "I want this `.md` to render when I visit it in Chrome":

```
1. User navigates to file:///path/to/foo.md
2. Chrome loads the page with default text/plain handling
3. Our content script (handler.ts) runs at document_end
   - url matches /\.(md|mdx|markdown|json|jsonc)(\?.*)?(#.*)?$/i
   - settings.formats[ext] enabled? (reads chrome.storage.sync)
   - sessionStorage["fv-handled"] === url? → bail (re-entry guard)
4. fetch(url) → raw file text
   - (fallback: document.querySelector("pre")?.textContent)
5. chrome.storage.session.set({ [key]: { url, content, name } })
6. location.replace(chrome-extension://…/src/app/index.html?intercept=<key>)
7. Viewer tab loads; App.tsx pickupIntercept() reads the key
8. intercept.ts builds LibraryFile { id: "intercept:<url>", sourceUrl, content }
9. addFiles + setActive → the file appears in the library + tab strip
10. urlSync rewrites ?intercept=<key> → ?file=<id> (shareable)
```

**Requires** the user to have enabled "Allow access to file URLs" on the
extension details page — Chrome gates that behind an explicit toggle per
extension.

## 9. FSA (File System Access) lifecycle

Chrome's FSA permission model:

- **Handle**: serializable via IDB (idb-keyval round-trips it). Survives
  browser restarts.
- **Permission**: NOT serializable. After a browser restart,
  `queryPermission` returns `"prompt"` and the user must re-grant via a
  user-gesture-driven `requestPermission` call.
- **Absolute path**: intentionally hidden. No API exposes
  `/Users/…/folder`. This is why "Open in editor" / "Reveal in Finder"
  need a user-pasted `rootPath` on FSA folders.

### Silent auto-restore (app boot)

`App.tsx` on mount: for every `LibraryFolder` in the store, try
`trySilentRestore(folder)`:

```
loadDirHandle(folder.handleId)  ← pulls from IDB
queryPermissionState(handle)    ← no gesture needed
  "granted"  → walkDirectory, register session handles → sessionRev bumps
  anything else → leave "Reconnect folder" button visible
```

When the user clicks **Reconnect folder**, `restoreFolder()` calls
`requestPermission` (user gesture OK), walks the dir, and registers
session handles.

## 10. Tabs + URL sync + hash nav

### Tabs

- `openTabs: string[]` in `useLibrary`. Stable order: a file keeps its
  slot once added. `setActive(id)` appends the id if new; never
  reorders.
- `closeTab(id)`: removes id, activates the tab to its right (then
  left, then null). Matches VS Code.
- `TabStrip.tsx` scrolls the active tab into view on change via
  `data-tab-id="<id>"` attribute matching + `CSS.escape`.
- On hydrate, any tab id that no longer has a backing file is filtered
  out (defense against stale IDB state).

### URL sync (`urlSync.ts`)

Two-way, runs once post-hydrate + on every `popstate`:

```
URL → store:  read ?file=<id>; if files[id] exists and differs from
              active, setActive(id)
store → URL:  on activeFileId change, history.replaceState writes
              ?file=<id>, strips transient ?intercept=<key>, preserves #hash
```

`replaceState` (not `pushState`) — no extra history entries per tab
click.

### Hash nav (MDX side)

- `rehype-slug` adds `id` to every heading.
- `MDXViewer` on mount/body-change: if `location.hash` is set, queue a
  microtask to `getElementById(slug)?.scrollIntoView`.
- TOC entry click: `e.preventDefault()` + `scrollIntoView` + `history.
  replaceState("", "", "#slug")` so copy-pasteable URLs round-trip.

Combined: `chrome-extension://…/index.html?file=X#heading` opens file X
and scrolls to `#heading`.

## 11. Rendering pipelines

### Markdown / MDX (`@filemark/mdx`)

#### Why `react-markdown` and not `@mdx-js/mdx`

The package is named `@filemark/mdx` but internally it's `react-markdown`
+ a stack of remark/rehype plugins — **not** `@mdx-js/mdx`. This was a
constrained choice, not a preference:

1. **MV3 CSP forbids `unsafe-eval` on extension pages.** The browser
   rejects `eval()` / `new Function()` / `setTimeout("string")` with a
   `EvalError: Refused to evaluate a string as JavaScript` the moment
   they run on any page whose origin is `chrome-extension://…`.
2. **`@mdx-js/mdx`'s evaluate path requires eval.** Its `evaluate` /
   `run` helpers compile MDX source → a JavaScript function via
   `new Function(...)` at runtime. That's eval. Hard stop on extension
   pages.
3. **MV3 won't let us opt out.** The `content_security_policy
   .extension_pages` manifest field in MV3 accepts only `'self'`,
   `'none'`, `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and localhost dev URLs. `'unsafe-eval'`
   is not on that list — a deliberate Chrome tightening from MV2 → MV3.
4. **Build-time compile doesn't help.** MDX's `compile()` emits static
   JS, which runs fine under CSP — but that's only useful for MDX files
   you ship *with* the extension. Filemark's whole point is that a user
   drops any `.md` / `.mdx` file at runtime, so we need a dynamic path.

What `react-markdown` gives us instead:

- Zero eval. AST walk → React element tree. Pure function.
- Plugin ecosystem already covers the real needs: `remark-gfm` (tables,
  task lists), `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` (LaTeX), `remark-breaks`
  (single-newline paragraphs), `rehype-raw` (arbitrary HTML tags pass
  through), `rehype-slug` (heading anchors).
- **Custom components via lowercase HTML tags.** Because `rehype-raw`
  lets `<callout>`, `<datagrid>`, `<tabs>` through as hast elements,
  `react-markdown`'s `components` map gives us MDX-flavored component
  dispatch without the MDX runtime. See `MDXViewer.tsx` `components`
  map. `<Datagrid src="…">` is handled this way.
- **Fenced info-strings are preserved.** Our `remark-code-meta` plugin
  copies `node.meta` onto the hast code element as `data-meta` so the
  custom `code` component can read the `type:<col>=…` flags on a
  ` ```csv ` fence.

What we lose vs real MDX:

- **No JSX expressions.** `{count * 2}` in markdown is literal text,
  not a JS expression. Attribute values on HTML-like tags are strings
  only (so e.g. `data={[1,2,3]}` in a `<Datagrid>` tag cannot work —
  the value is the four-character string `"[1,"`).
- **No `import` / `export` in the document.** The document is data,
  not code.

Workarounds already shipped:

- `<Datagrid src="…" meta="type:priority=status(P0:danger)" />` is the
  MDX-component equivalent for datagrids. All "JS-ish" logic lives in
  string attributes; the component interprets them.
- For inline data that's too awkward to express as attributes (CSV with
  commas, newlines), fall back to a ` ```csv ` fenced block.

Deferred (v0.2+): a **sandbox iframe** (`content_security_policy.sandbox`
lets `'unsafe-eval'` through inside an isolated page that has no
`chrome.*` APIs) could host `@mdx-js/mdx`'s `evaluate` and talk to the
main app via `postMessage`. That's the only path that unlocks real MDX
JSX. Sidebar of PROBLEM.md notes this as a stretch. Not on the v0.1
surface.

#### Pipeline

```
source ─▶ extractFrontmatter (yaml pkg) ─▶ body
        ─▶ <Frontmatter data=…>          ─▶ card above body

body ─▶ react-markdown(
           remarkPlugins: [remarkGfm, remarkMath, remarkBreaks]
           rehypePlugins: [rehypeRaw, rehypeSlug, rehypeKatex]
           components: { code → Mermaid if lang === "mermaid" else CodeBlock,
                         input → TaskCheckbox,
                         a → SmartLink,
                         img → SmartImage,
                         callout → Callout,
                         tabs/tab → Tabs/Tab,
                         details → Details }
        )
```

- `Mermaid` lazy-imports the `mermaid` package (~800 KB) — Vite code-
  splits it so diagram-free files don't pay the cost. Theme picked from
  the host: `dark` mode → `dark`, `sepia` → `neutral`, else `default`.
  `mermaid.parse()` runs before `render()` so syntax errors surface as
  a styled error card instead of unmounting the document.

- `remark-breaks` preserves single newlines → ASCII trees / flow diagrams
  don't collapse into one paragraph.
- `rehype-raw` parses HTML in markdown so `<Callout type="tip">…` works
  as a component tag (the markdown-parsed lowercase `<callout>` maps to
  our component via `components.callout`).
- `CodeBlock` promotes multi-line inline code (single backticks spanning
  lines) to block rendering so whitespace is preserved.
- `TaskCheckbox` strips `remark-gfm`'s hard-coded `disabled` so the box
  is interactive; persists checked state via injected `StorageAdapter`
  under `fv:task:<fileId>`.
- Shiki runs through our `shiki.ts` in-package helper: `shiki/core` +
  JavaScript regex engine + per-language dynamic imports. Avoids the
  ~3 MB bundle the default `import "shiki"` produces (Rollup statically
  resolves its dynamic imports).
- TOC: after render, scan `rootRef.current.querySelectorAll("h1,h2,h3,
  h4")`, build a `{id, text, depth}[]`. Hidden via a host-level
  `data-toc="closed"` attribute + CSS — package stays UI-state unaware.

### JSON / JSONC (`@file-viewer/json`)

```
source ─▶ parseJSON (jsonc-parser) ─▶ { value, errors, strict }

value ─▶ renderJsonTree(
           guards for undefined / null / primitive roots,
           JSONErrorBoundary
           ─▶ <JsonView value theme … />  (@uiw/react-json-view)
         )
```

- `jsonc-parser`: tolerant of `//` + `/* */` comments and trailing commas.
- Strict-mode detection: if the source also parses with native
  `JSON.parse`, `strict: true` → shows a "valid" pill; else "jsonc"
  pill. Parse errors render in an expandable details strip with line /
  column info.
- Theme: picks one of nine bundled themes
  (`githubDark` / `githubLight` / `nord` / `vscode` / `basic` / `dark`
  / `light` / `monokai` / `gruvbox`) via `options.theme` or follows host
  `ThemeProvider.mode` when `theme: "auto"`.
- Large-file threshold (1 MB): renders collapsed at depth 1 with a hint
  to switch to Raw.

### Datagrid (`@filemark/datagrid`)

Interactive table rendering — consumed by `@filemark/mdx` (for fenced
data blocks + opted-in GFM tables) and (v0.2+) `@filemark/csv` for
standalone `.csv` / `.tsv` files. Headless core = TanStack Table +
TanStack Virtual; input shape `{columns, rows}`; zero host / platform
imports.

**Authoring inside markdown — one syntax, three sources of data:**

````md
# (a) inline data — the default. csv/tsv parsed from block body.
```csv filter=false sort=age:desc
name,age,role
Ada,30,eng
Grace,45,admiral
```

# (b) external file — empty body, `src=` resolves via AssetResolver.
```csv src=./sales.csv hide=internal_id
```

# (c) GFM table upgrade — HTML comment hint before a plain table.
<!-- datagrid sort=qty:desc -->
| item | qty |
|------|-----|
| pens | 12  |
````

No MDX JSX components: `@filemark/mdx` is built on `react-markdown`
(CSP bans `unsafe-eval` → `@mdx-js/mdx` off the table). Interception
happens in `components.code` for ` ```csv `, ` ```tsv `, ` ```datagrid `
langs, and in `components.table` for the GFM-comment-hint path.

**Info-string grammar** (` ```csv <flag> <flag=value> ... `):

| Flag | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `filter` | on | `filter=false` to disable per-column filter row |
| `sort` | on | `sort=<col>[:asc|desc]` sets initial sort; `sort=false` disables |
| `search` | on | global search box; `search=false` hides |
| `hide` | — | comma-list of columns to omit (`hide=id,internal`) |
| `type:<col>` | inferred | `type:age=number` / `type:joined=date` forces a parse |
| `align:<col>` | inferred | `align:price=right` |
| `delimiter` | `,` (csv) / `\t` (tsv) | per-block override (`delimiter=;`) |
| `header` | on | `header=false` → synthesize `col_0`, `col_1`, … |
| `src` | — | relative path; resolved via `AssetResolver` (see below) |
| `height` | auto | px height for virtualized body |

Unknown flags → console warn + render (Rule 3 — no silent fallback).

**Pipeline:**

```
react-markdown
  components.code (lang ∈ {csv, tsv, datagrid})
    ├─ parseInfoString(meta)           →  DataGridOptions
    ├─ opts.src ? assets.resolve(src)  →  blob: / https: URL → fetch
    │            : codeBlockChildren   →  inline text
    ├─ papaparse(text, delimiter)      →  { columns, rows }
    ├─ inferTypes(sample rows)         →  per-col num | date | bool | str
    └─ <DataGrid columns rows options/>
```

`@filemark/datagrid` ships only the last step (headless table UI +
inline-md cell renderer). Parse + type inference + MDX wiring lives in
`@filemark/mdx`. This keeps the datagrid pkg reusable by
`@filemark/csv`, `@filemark/json` (array-of-objects), and any future
VS Code / web-demo host.

**Cell renderer:** each cell runs through an inline-markdown pass
(bold, code, link, strikethrough, task-list checkbox) via a minimal
remark subset — not full block md (no nested lists / code blocks —
breaks row-height virtualization).

**Persisted grid state:** sort / filter / hidden columns key off
`StorageAdapter` under `filemark:datagrid:<fileId>:<blockIndex>`.
Reuses the same adapter that drives task-list checkbox persistence.

### AssetResolver (relative-path resolution)

`AssetResolver` is the host-injected interface viewers use whenever a
markdown body references a sibling file — `![alt](./diagram.png)`,
` ```csv src=./data.csv `, and future patterns (linked `.md`, embedded
`.svg`). Viewers never know whether they're in Chrome, VS Code, or a
web demo; they just call `assets.resolve(relPath)` and get back a URL
they can assign to `<img src>` or pass to `fetch()`.

**Interface** (defined in `@filemark/core`):

```ts
export interface AssetResolver {
  resolve(relativePath: string, baseUrl?: string): Promise<string>;
}
```

Returns a URL string — either a `blob:` (for locally-read bytes) or a
remote `https:` / `file:` URL. Callers must not assume either form.

**Four implementations — picked by file ingest kind:**

| Host context | Implementation | `resolve()` does |
|---|---|---|
| FSA folder (`kind: "fsa"`) | `FSAAssetResolver` | walks the `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` by path segments (`./img/foo.png` → `img/` sub-handle → `foo.png` file-handle → `File` → `URL.createObjectURL`). Caches blob URLs per (dir-handle, path). |
| Drop-folder (`kind: "drop"`) | `DropAssetResolver` | looks up an in-memory `Map<relativePath, File>` populated at drop time from `items[].webkitGetAsEntry()` recursion. Returns `URL.createObjectURL(file)`. |
| `file://` intercept | `PassthroughResolver` | returns `new URL(relativePath, sourceUrl).toString()` — the browser fetches via `file://`, which **works for images but not for CSV reads** (same-origin rules on file://). Datagrid `src=` refuses to fetch and renders a warning. |
| Remote (`raw.github*`, etc.) | `PassthroughResolver` | same — `new URL(relativePath, sourceUrl)`. Works for CSV fetch if the host permission covers the origin. |

**Lifecycle of a blob URL:**

- Created on first `resolve()` call; cached per viewer-instance until tab close.
- Revoked when the owning tab unmounts (tab close or viewer swap). Avoids leaking object URLs across long sessions.
- `FSAAssetResolver` re-reads on handle-permission change (FSA handles can go stale if the folder is ejected and re-granted).

**Datagrid-specific handling of `src=`:**

1. `opts.src` present → call `assets.resolve(opts.src, sourceUrl)`.
2. If resolver throws `ENOENT`-ish (file missing or handle gone) → render an inline error card, not an empty grid. Rule 3 — skeletons must warn.
3. If resolver is `undefined` (single-file ingest has no siblings) → same error card with "open as folder to use `src=`" hint.
4. On success → `fetch(url).then(r => r.text())` → Papaparse → DataGrid.
5. No retry, no auto-reload. Re-render on file change is a stretch-goal tied to auto-refresh (§14).

**Security note:** the resolver is same-origin by convention. It MUST
refuse paths that escape the root (e.g. `../../..`). `FSAAssetResolver`
gets this for free (relative segments are walked against the directory
handle; `..` either fails or stays within the granted root). Passthrough
resolvers must `new URL()`-normalize and reject protocols other than
the one of `baseUrl`.

## 12. Theme system

One context, three surfaces:

```
useLibrary.theme ─▶ ThemeProvider (controlled)
                    ─▶ writes data-theme on <html>
                    ─▶ writes --fv-font-family / --fv-font-size /
                       --fv-line-height / --fv-content-width to <html>
                    ─▶ ALSO sets html.style.fontFamily + body.style.fontFamily
                       directly (survives Tailwind v4 preflight under
                       MV3 CSP where @layer resolution can differ)
```

- Three modes: `light` (default), `dark`, `sepia`. Each defines the
  shadcn token palette (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, …)
  in `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css`.
- shadcn's `.dark` variant is remapped to `[data-theme="dark"]` via
  `@custom-variant dark (&:is([data-theme="dark"], …))` so every
  `dark:` utility in the shadcn component files works without an extra
  class on `<html>`.
- Theme popover lives in `shell/ThemePopover.tsx`. Sliders +
  segmented controls + reset-to-defaults button. Settings persist via
  `useLibrary.setTheme` → IDB.

## 13. Shortcut system

Chrome extensions running on `chrome-extension://` pages can only
reliably intercept **bare keys with no modifiers**. Every `⌘`, `Ctrl`,
and `Alt` combo we tried is claimed by Chrome at the browser level:

- `⌘1–9` / `Alt+1–9` / `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` / `⌘⇧]` / `⌘⇧[` /
  `⌘W` all switch Chrome's own tabs, not ours.
- `preventDefault()` in page JS cannot override browser-level chords.

Current scheme (all gated on `!isInInput(e)` so typing is safe):

| Chord | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `]` | next tab |
| `[` | prev tab |
| `x` | close active tab |
| `1`–`9` | jump to tab N |
| `f` | fullscreen |
| `r` | rendered ↔ raw |
| `\` | toggle TOC |
| `/` | focus folder filter |
| `⌘K` | search (Chrome leaves `⌘K` alone) |
| `⌘B` | toggle sidebar (Chrome leaves this too) |
| `Esc` | close overlays / exit fullscreen |

Every chord maps to a `ShortcutId` in `settings.ts` → togglable per-
shortcut on the options page. Master "Disable all shortcuts" flag in
the same store.

## 14. Auto-refresh

`Viewer.tsx` polling loop — active only when:

1. `useLibrary.autoRefresh === true`, **and**
2. The active file is refreshable — `fileIsRefreshable(file, handles)`
   is true when:
   - folder file with a live session handle, OR
   - file with a `sourceUrl` starting with `file://` (fetchable from
     the extension page if "Allow access to file URLs" is on)

On each tick (`autoRefreshMs`, default 2000 ms):
- Read latest via handle or `fetch(sourceUrl)`
- Compare to `contentRef.current` — only `setContent(next)` if changed
  (no re-render for no-op)
- Silent failure on a single tick; next tick retries

Viewer effect is keyed by `file?.id` + `sessionRev`, not the `file`
object, so mutating `lastOpenedAt` on the files map doesn't trigger a
reload flash.

## 15. Raw view

`RawView.tsx` shows the file source exactly as it sits on disk:

- Runs the same `highlight()` from `@file-viewer/mdx`'s Shiki pipeline
  (same grammars + themes the MDX code blocks use). Read-only — Monaco
  is deferred to a later milestone (MV3 CSP + bundle cost).
- `ext → lang` mapping in `extToLang()` so `.md` uses `markdown`, `.tsx`
  uses `tsx`, etc.
- Wrap toggle (session-only): `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words` when
  on, `overflow-x-auto` + `whitespace-pre` when off.
- Copy button copies the raw content to the clipboard.
- Reached via the `R` shortcut or FileActions menu.

## 16. Options page

`apps/chrome-ext/src/options/OptionsApp.tsx`. Four sections:

1. **File formats** — toggles per-format interception + drop acceptance.
2. **JSON viewer** — theme, collapsed depth, shorten length, indent,
   data-type display, object-size display, clipboard icons. Applied
   live to the Viewer via `useSettings.settings.json`.
3. **Keyboard shortcuts** — per-shortcut switches + master disable.
4. **Reset to defaults** — wipes settings only, leaves library intact.

Settings are written to `chrome.storage.sync` (cross-profile) with IDB
fallback. The viewer tab picks up changes live via
`chrome.storage.onChanged`.

## 17. Security / CSP

- **MV3 default extension-page CSP**: `script-src 'self'; object-src
  'self';`. No `unsafe-eval` allowed, no remote scripts, no inline
  scripts. This drove:
  - Markdown via `react-markdown` (no eval path) instead of
    `@mdx-js/mdx`'s `evaluate()`
  - `yaml` (pure JS) instead of `gray-matter` (Node-dep bloat)
  - Shiki via `shiki/core` + JS regex engine (no WASM eval)
- **Content scripts** are classic scripts — no `import` statements. The
  build outputs `content.js` as a single-line IIFE.
- **Service worker** is a module (`"type": "module"`). Uses
  `import.meta.env.MODE` for dev/prod branch.
- **Sandboxed iframe** is available but not used yet; reserved for
  `@mdx-js/mdx`'s `evaluate()` (true MDX JSX expressions) and
  Monaco / CodeMirror edit mode.

### `host_permissions: ["<all_urls>"]`

The manifest grants broad host access so `fetch()` from extension pages
(the viewer tab and options page) can bypass CORS — required for
`<Datagrid src="https://…" />` and ` ```csv src=https://… ` to load
arbitrary remote CSVs. Without this, browsers block responses that
lack `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

- **Trade-off accepted for v0.1.** The Chrome Web Store install prompt
  now reads "Read and change your data on all websites". For a doc
  viewer this is broad. Justified by the feature's usefulness (load any
  public CSV), the fact that the extension only *fetches* data (it
  never exfiltrates, injects scripts, or writes to external hosts), and
  the lack of a less-scary mechanism in MV3 that still bypasses CORS.
- **Planned follow-up (Option B).** Move to `optional_host_permissions`
  + an in-UI "Grant access to {origin}" button surfaced inside the
  datagrid error card when a fetch fails. Requires:
  1. Swap `host_permissions` → `optional_host_permissions` in manifest.
  2. Add a `PermissionAdapter { hasHostAccess, requestHostAccess }`
     interface in `@filemark/core`.
  3. Implement it in `apps/chrome-ext/src/app/adapters/` using
     `chrome.permissions.{contains,request}`.
  4. Thread it through `ViewerProps` alongside `storage` + `assets`.
  5. `DataBlock` catches CORS errors, shows a Grant button, retries on
     success.
  - Net effect: the install prompt goes back to just `"storage"`; users
    hit a prompt only when they actually load an external URL, and only
    for that origin. Tracked in `TASKS.md` as the follow-up to M7.

## 18. Data lifecycle (hydrate → runtime → persist)

```
App.tsx on mount
 ├─ useLibrary.hydrate()         ← all lib:* IDB keys in parallel
 │    └─ filters orphan tabs
 │    └─ restores ui prefs
 ├─ useSettings.hydrate()        ← chrome.storage.sync first, IDB fallback
 │    └─ registers onChanged listener
 ├─ trySilentRestore(each folder) ← silent FSA permission check
 │    └─ sessionHandles.register on success
 │    └─ useLibrary.setState({ sessionRev: sessionRev + 1 })
 └─ pickupIntercept()
      └─ if ?intercept=<key>: read from chrome.storage.session
      └─ materialize intercept-file, addFiles, setActive
      └─ history.replaceState strips ?intercept=
```

Runtime:

- Every `setActive(id)` writes `lib:active` immediately; updates the
  `files` map (`lastOpenedAt`); openTabs on first add; recent on first
  add. Guard: same-id calls early-return without mutation.
- Every `toggleSidebar/Toc/Fullscreen/AutoRefresh` writes
  `lib:ui` after the state flip.
- Every `setTheme` patch writes `lib:theme`.
- Every task-checkbox change writes `fv:task:<fileId>`.

## 19. Known constraints

| Limitation | Reason | Workaround |
| --- | --- | --- |
| True MDX JSX expressions (`{count * 2}`) | MV3 strict CSP blocks `unsafe-eval` | HTML-tag components only for now; sandbox iframe path for a later milestone |
| FSA folder absolute path hidden | Chrome security | User pastes `rootPath` once per folder, or uses file:// interception |
| Tab shortcuts limited to bare keys | Chrome claims every Ctrl/⌘/Alt combo at the browser level | Vim-style no-modifier chords, gated on not-in-input |
| Monaco editor | ~3 MB gzipped + worker / CSP collisions | Shiki for read-only today; CodeMirror 6 is the planned editable path |
| VS Code–style chord rebinding UI | Requires keymap + chord capture + conflict detection | v0.3+ feature; current options page has on/off per shortcut only |
| Single-tab Chrome process cache | Extension code caches aggressively between reloads | After every `pnpm build`, reload the extension card at `chrome://extensions` |

## 20. Adding a new feature — checklist

Use this as a pre-flight before you commit:

1. **Where does it live?**
   - Pure / host-agnostic content rendering → viewer package
     (`packages/<name>-viewer`)
   - App chrome (topbar / sidebar / tab strip / shortcuts) → host
     (`apps/chrome-ext/src/app`)
   - Options / settings → `settings.ts` + `OptionsApp.tsx`

2. **Does it touch storage?**
   - Library state → new key in `KEYS` in `store.ts`, added to
     `hydrate()` + relevant persist paths
   - User settings → new field in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` + patch / setter in
     `settings.ts` + option control in `OptionsApp.tsx`

3. **Does it introduce a new format?**
   - Add to `ALL_FORMATS` in `settings.ts`
   - Add to `FORMAT_META` in `OptionsApp.tsx`
   - Add to `EXT_MAP` in `registry.ts`
   - Extend `SUPPORTED` regex in `content/handler.ts`
   - Extend `extToLang` in `RawView.tsx`
   - Pass per-format options down through `Viewer.tsx` if the viewer
     exposes options

4. **Does it add a shortcut?**
   - Add a `ShortcutId` + entry to `ALL_SHORTCUTS` in `settings.ts`
   - Wire handler in `Shell.tsx:onKey`, gated by `isShortcutEnabled`
     and (for bare keys) `!isInInput(e)`
   - Remember: Chrome claims every Ctrl/⌘/Alt combo — bare keys only

5. **Does it render custom DOM content?**
   - For MDX viewer additions: keep it package-local and Tailwind-only
     (don't add CSS to the host stylesheet). For runtime-exported
     components, wrap in the MDX `components` map.
   - For shell additions: Tailwind utilities + shadcn tokens
     (`bg-muted`, `text-foreground`, …). Never raw color literals.

6. **Does it add a new basecn / shadcn primitive?**
   - Run `pnpm --filter chrome-ext dlx shadcn@latest add
     https://basecn.dev/r/<name>.json`
   - If the shipped `<Name>Content` is a bare `Popup`, wrap it with
     `Portal + Positioner` locally (Base UI error #71). Our existing
     Tooltip / Popover / DropdownMenu components are already patched.
   - Prefer `children` over `render={<…/>}` on triggers — nesting
     providers inside `render` is error #31 territory.

7. **Build + reload.** Every structural edit:
   ```bash
   pnpm --filter '@file-viewer/*' build   # viewer packages
   pnpm --filter chrome-ext build
   ```
   Then reload the card at `chrome://extensions`.

8. **Commit.** Short subject, grouped bullet body, no
   Claude/AI/Anthropic references. Never push without asking.
